fields.meta_title: Construction Quote Form Builder for Contractors | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a construction quote form that collects site photos and measurements, prices jobs from your own rates, and lets customers sign to accept.
fields.h1: Build a Construction Quote Form That Prices Each Job
fields.hero_description: Build a construction quote form that collects measurements and site photos, then prices the job from your own rates.
fields.features_heading: What a Construction Quote Request Carries
fields.features_subheading: A callback for missing measurements delays every price. This form takes them up front, prices the job, and gets the quote signed.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that follow the job type

Pick a kitchen remodel and the form asks for the room size and the feet of cabinets. Pick a driveway and it asks for the length and width and whether an old slab comes out.
fields.feature_2:
Photos and plans attached to the request

Customers add site photos from a phone and upload floor plans or sketches with the request. The estimator opens one record that holds every file next to the customer's measurements.
fields.feature_3:
A price on screen from your rates

Enter your own rate per square foot or per item, and the form multiplies it by the customer's measurements. The customer sees the estimate on screen, marked subject to a site visit.
fields.feature_4:
Each request routed to the right estimator

Route requests by trade or by size. A fit-out over a set square footage goes to the senior estimator in a Slack message, and smaller jobs go to the shared estimating queue.
fields.feature_5:
Quotes accepted with a signature

Send the itemized quote back to the customer as a page with every line and the total. The customer signs on a phone to accept, and the signed quote saves with the original request.
fields.feature_6:
Every request in a database you own

Each request and its signed quote save as rows in a database you own, with no cap on responses. Sort open quotes by value or estimator to see which ones are still waiting.

fields.tab_content_1:
The estimator sees 3 kitchen photos before the site walk

Gretchen Albers wants her kitchen redone and fills out the Corvallo Remodeling quote form on her phone. She enters a 12 by 14 foot room, 18 feet of cabinets, and her address, then adds 3 photos. Estimator Tobias Kwan gets the request by email and books the site walk for Thursday.
fields.tab_content_2:
Two measurements turn into a $7,920 driveway price

Tollgate Concrete prices driveways at $9 a square foot for a new pour and $2 a square foot to remove an old slab. Hadley Voss enters 24 by 30 feet and checks that her old slab comes out. The form shows 720 square feet, $6,480 for the pour and $1,440 for removal, or $7,920 pending a site visit.
fields.tab_content_3:
With the floor plan, a 5,200-square-foot suite reaches Bastian

Requests at Brightquay Builders come from tenants fitting out leased space. Venn Pediatrics asks for a quote on a 5,200-square-foot suite and uploads its floor plan. Any fit-out over 4,000 square feet goes to senior estimator Bastian Roe in a Slack direct message. Smaller requests stay in the general estimating queue.
fields.tab_content_4:
Accepted from his phone, then on the schedule

Paul Dekker opens his quote from Pellwick Basements on his phone: framing at $6,200, drywall at $4,800, electrical at $3,900, and flooring at $5,100, or $20,000 in all. He signs to accept it. Project manager Ruben Iyer gets an email that the quote is signed and puts the job on the schedule.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Construction Quote Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build a construction quote form that collects each job's measurements and prices them from your own rates.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the jobs you quote most
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for the numbers you price from
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pull up your last year of quotes and group them by job, such as kitchens, driveways, or tenant fit-outs. Each group becomes a job type on the form with its own questions. A driveway customer then never sees a cabinet field.
fields.howto_step_2_des: For each job type, write down the measurements you multiply by a rate: square feet of slab, feet of cabinets, or the size of a suite. Ask for exactly those, and put the unit next to each field.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Enter the rate behind each line, such as one price per square foot to pour and another to tear out. Keep the rates in one table. A price change next spring then updates every estimate the form shows.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Add a photo upload for the rooms or the site and a file upload for floor plans. Name the shots you want, such as each wall of a kitchen. The estimator can then plan the site walk before arriving.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Route by trade or by size. Set the square footage or job value that sends a request to a senior estimator, and send the rest to a shared estimating inbox. Each request arrives as an email or a Slack message.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Before sharing the link, submit 3 requests yourself: a small job, one slightly over your routing threshold, and one without photos. Check that each estimate matches your own math on paper and that each request reaches the right estimator.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Send the itemized quote to sign
fields.howto_step_7_des: Once the estimator settles the price, send the customer the itemized quote to review line by line and sign on a phone. The project manager schedules the crew from the signed version, not from a draft that changed twice.

faq_plan.q: What is a construction quote form?
faq_plan.a: A construction quote form is the form a contractor's customers fill out to request a price for a job. It records the job type, the measurements, the site address, and photos or plans, and it can show an estimate from the contractor's own rates before anyone visits the site.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a construction quote form?
faq_plan.a: List the jobs you quote, the measurements each one is priced from, and your rates. In Emergent's AI form builder, describe it in one prompt, such as "patios at $14 a square foot, with a photo upload." Emergent builds the form and its estimate, with a database for every request.

faq_plan.q: What should a construction quote form ask for?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the customer's name and phone number, the site address, the job type, and the measurements you price from. Add a photo upload and the start date they want. Ask for a budget range only when your price changes with the finish level, such as stock or custom cabinets.

faq_plan.q: When should a construction quote form lead to a full proposal instead?
faq_plan.a: Move to a proposal when the customer is still choosing between approaches, materials, or schedules. A quote fits a settled scope where the customer mainly needs the price. For open-ended jobs, write a proposal and collect the project details on a proposal form first.

faq_plan.q: Can a construction quote form calculate a price on its own?
faq_plan.a: Yes, from rates you set. The form multiplies each measurement by your price for that line, such as square feet of tile, and adds up the lines. Label the result as an estimate pending a site visit. With Emergent, you change a rate later by asking for the change in a prompt.

faq_plan.q: How do I add photo and plan uploads to a construction quote form?
faq_plan.a: Add a photo field that opens the phone's camera and a file field for floor plans or drawings. Tell customers which shots to take, such as the whole room and any damage up close. Each file saves with the request, and the estimator sees it before the site walk.

faq_plan.q: Can a construction quote form handle commercial bid requests?
faq_plan.a: Yes, for jobs with a clear scope, like a tenant fit-out priced by the square foot. When an owner wants formal bids from several contractors against one set of drawings and a due date, set that up as an RFP form instead.

faq_plan.q: How long should the price from a construction quote form stay valid?
faq_plan.a: Pick a window you can hold your material and labor prices for, such as 30 days, and print the expiry date on the quote. When the date passes before the customer signs, the app can email the estimator a reminder to reprice the job.

faq_plan.q: Do construction quote forms work for both residential and commercial jobs?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when each job type gets its own questions. A homeowner remodeling a kitchen answers about rooms and cabinets, while a commercial tenant gives the suite size and uploads a floor plan. Emergent builds both paths from one prompt, and both save to the same database you own.

faq_plan.q: How do I keep construction quote form requests apart from other inquiries?
faq_plan.a: Give each kind of inquiry its own form and its own inbox. Quote requests go to estimating, warranty calls go to service, and requests for the company to back a local youth team go on a sponsorship form. Forms built with Emergent have no response caps.

plan.angle: Wave 3 page with no top 10 in the workbook, and the AlsoAsked pull drifts into quote templates and inspirational quotes, so the page wins on depth for a contractor building the form: the fields that change by job type, photos and plans attached to the request, a price computed from the contractor's own rates, routing by job size to the right estimator, and the customer accepting the itemized quote with a signature. Four construction jobs a contractor will recognize: a kitchen remodel, a concrete driveway, a commercial tenant fit-out, and a basement finish. The FAQ answers the definition and how to build one, then the questions a contractor setting one up asks: what to ask, pricing on screen, attachments, quote versus proposal, commercial bids, validity windows, follow-up and keeping other inquiries out of the estimator's queue.

findings.quote: These six parts collect what the estimator needs the first time.
findings.issue: An each/every claim about the six features that is false for most of them (rework-checklist 7, Divit 2026-11-03): feature_3 'A price on screen from your rates' shows the customer an estimate, feature_4 'Each request routed to the right estimator' routes, feature_5 'Quotes accepted with a signature' collects the customer's acceptance after pricing, and feature_6 'Every request in a database you own' stores. Only features 1 and 2 collect what the estimator needs. No other each/all claim on the page is false (checked H1, howto_description, why_description, every feature and step).
findings.fix: Drop the 'six parts collect' claim and describe the form as a whole, e.g. 'The form asks for the measurements and photos up front, prices the job from your rates and gets the signed quote back.'
